judges: Sanjay K. Agrawal C.A.V. Judgment J.
case_name: Loknath Died Through Lrs. Shribachahh ... vs Sindhu

parties.respondent_defendant: Sindhu, W/o Akhil Kolta, Aged about 60 years, R/o Vill. Thenga Gudi, P.S. Saria, Teh. Sarangarh, Distt. Raigarh (C.G.)

facts_of_case: Loknath's legal representatives filed a second appeal against Sindhu and others.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party claiming a partition to prove that it has taken place.
legal_principles.held: It is the case of the plaintiff that since the suit property was undivided amongst Mohan, Abhiram, Goverdhan & Jeeverdhan and since Ghasi died in the year 1942, defendants No.1 & 2 would get no share in the property being governed by clause 29 of the Raigarh State Wajib-ul-arz.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has remarried in chudi form is not entitled to a share in the joint family property.
legal_principles.held: Defendant No.1 after the death of Ghasi in the year 1942, remained in the village and stayed in the house left by Ghasi and she never remarried, though she left the village for some time, but she never remarried

outcome.final_order: The final court order is not specified in the provided judgment excerpt.

use_for_drafting: Second appeals in Hindu Succession Act cases
